response.markdown_report:
**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Positive–negative margins measure discrimination against supplied negatives, not calibrated relevance or HR@10. Scale changes can improve margins without improving ranking. (2) Existing probes never perturb histories. They cannot establish whether older interactions outweigh coherent recent behavior. (3) Positionwise training scores do not verify inference readout. Left-padded histories require the final nonpadding position, never `count−1`.

**Insights from related work.** (1) NextItNet’s dilated convolutions expand architectural reach [1], but exact dependencies require auditing convolution paths and normalization axes [4]. Reach differs from measured sensitivity. (2) Interaction-removal research motivates temporal probes [2], while ROAR distinguishes frozen-model ablation from retraining [5]. Padding replacement can introduce artifacts. (3) Usage-centric intent research separates intended use from superficial similarity [3]. Titles and descriptions cannot establish satisfaction, compatibility, or unmet needs.

**Directions and framework.** Retain three axes: structural correctness, temporal sensitivity, and semantic evidence. Their observations are readout/dependency checks, controlled paired prediction changes, and text-supported relation labels. Missing evidence remains unknown; none directly measures latent intent.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/future potential/code difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Assessments apply to each dimension in order.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Controlled position-preserving lag ablation [1,2,4,5] | 4/6/5 | Useful integration; guides temporal hypotheses; existing hooks suffice | Established technique; predictive value uncertain; controls require care |
| Occasional contiguous older-prefix dropout [1,2] | 4/6/4 | Simple combination; feasible regularizer; small training change | Modest novelty; useful history may disappear; predictor consistency needs checks |
| Abstaining title/description relation audit [3] | 5/6/6 | Distinct evidence schema; interpretable findings; no fitted ensemble | Limited novelty; sparse text limits validation; annotation effort remains |

**Selected idea: controlled position-preserving lag diagnosis.** At 0% progress, diagnose before modifying training. Freeze each category’s single corrected NextItNet. Define lag zero as the final observed item, preserve it and the original readout, and perturb only originally occupied positive lags. Compare recent, old, and random positions with equal per-user replacement counts on identical eligible users. Include no-op, ID-0, explicit zero-embedding, and frequency-matched valid-item replacements; disagreement identifies intervention dependence, not user intent.

```text
freeze checkpoint, candidates, sequence width, and original readout
score intact histories; apply prespecified matched-count interventions
record paired score/rank changes, hit transitions, and top-10 overlap
aggregate counts, strata, missing reasons, and uncertainty
```

Audit padding embeddings, block activation norms, every temporal convolution, and normalization axes. Test outside-field invariance only when the complete graph guarantees locality. Use fixed validation candidates when available: report baseline/ablated HR@10 and paired percentage-point differences with category-stratified bootstrap intervals. Training-loader margins remain separate; omit unavailable rank metrics. Sampled results remain protocol-specific [6].

Preserve both diagnostic entry points, ModelView hooks, four routes, seeds, splits, and checkpoint/predictor consistency. Predeclare comparisons and limit exploratory selection to reduce adaptive validation overfitting. These controls cost additional inference; bound batches and repeats. Later dropout experiments must retain the NextItNet family and one checkpoint per category.

idea.description: Strengthen the position-preserving NextItNet lag-ablation diagnostic with matched replacement counts, padding and locality controls, fixed original readout, and paired uncertainty estimates. Measure each category’s single frozen model through the existing ModelView interface.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests stale or broadly related interests may displace specific recent matches, but the existing embedding and margin probes cannot verify that hypothesis. Controlled interventions can identify model sensitivity while distinguishing padding artifacts, positional effects, and unavailable evidence. They cannot establish user intent or prove that retraining without older interactions will improve recommendations.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data contracts. Use only histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions; keep unavailable category breakdowns empty and never infer ratings, review text, simulator traits, compatibility, or satisfaction.

Save and restore the actual module’s training mode; run deterministic evaluation without gradients except for an optional separate embedding-gradient probe. Keep item embedding sampling seeded at 42. Retain existing collapse and margin metrics with observation counts; an empty result must be explicitly missing with a reason, never a healthy-looking zero. Document that collapse is directional alignment and margins depend on score scale and supplied negatives.

Freeze the checkpoint, input width, candidate IDs, and original final nonpadding readout. For nonempty left-padded histories this is the final occupied index, never count−1. Exclude lag zero from interventions. For loader diagnostics, use the positive and negative aligned with that original index only when both are valid; count exclusions. Cache a bounded set of identical loader tuples before comparing conditions. Do not confuse these training sensitivity measurements with validation results.

Use a reproducible default protocol: up to ten cached loader batches; recent lags 1–5; old lags 16 and greater; history-length strata 1–5, 6–15, 16–31, and 32 or more. On each eligible history, choose m=min(3, recent-position count, old-position count), requiring m>=1. Draw m positions separately from recent, old, and all positive-lag occupied positions using fixed local RNG seed 42, with three repeated draws. Use the same selected positions across replacement types. Report realized lag distributions because random controls can overlap either band. These settings are proposed defaults, not empirically established optima.

Compare unchanged-history controls, ID-0 replacement, explicit zero input embeddings, and valid-item replacements. Form item-frequency quintiles from training interactions only, grouping tied frequencies together. Draw a different nonreserved item from the replaced item’s frequency bin, excluding the user’s observed training items and supplied candidates; abstain with a counted reason if no item qualifies. Repeated draws measure replacement variability, not additional independent users. Average repeated outcomes within user before aggregation.

Audit ID-0 weights and initialization, convolution biases, residual additions, and normalization axes. Explicit zero-embedding replacement needs an internal diagnostic forward path that preserves all subsequent operations; ID-0 replacement is not an equivalent substitute. A temporary embedding-output hook may implement this without changing the public ModelView API and must be removed in finally. Audit that this captures every input-embedding path. Inspect originally padded-position activation norms through successive blocks on bounded batches. Optional clamping after residual addition is a separately labeled mechanistic intervention, not an equivalent deletion.

Compute maximum convolutional span as R=1+sum((k−1)d) along the longest temporal path, counting both convolutions in applicable blocks; residual additions take dependency unions and dilations can leave holes. Claim outside-field invariance only after auditing every path, including normalization and global operations. Where applicable, replace originally occupied tokens at lags >=R while preserving the final R inputs. Compare final features and raw scores using disclosed dtype-aware tolerances; float32 defaults may use atol=1e-6 and rtol=1e-5. Changed outputs challenge the claimed locality or implementation. Unchanged outputs and zero gradients alone do not prove locality. Mark this control unavailable if no history extends beyond the field.

When authorized fixed validation candidates are exposed, retain exactly the host’s 200 users per category, target, 99 unique negatives, seed 42, and tie policy. Do not recreate a supposedly equivalent candidate set. Report baseline and intervened HR@10, paired changes in percentage points, hit-to-miss and miss-to-hit counts, target-rank changes, and top-10 set overlap |A∩B|/10. Report all-user results with ineligible histories unchanged, and eligible-only results separately with counts and strata. Use 2,000 paired user bootstrap replicates with local RNG seed 42: resample users jointly across conditions within each category and recompute the equal-weight four-category mean; report percentile 95% intervals. Intervals are conditional on checkpoints, candidates, and the realized replacement draws. They exclude training-seed and adaptive-search uncertainty. If candidates are unavailable through the adapter, omit these metrics and give explicit missing reasons.

Predeclare the main comparison as old versus random matched-count replacement under valid-item substitution; treat recent and padding comparisons as controls. Report prespecified and exploratory contrasts separately, without interpreting unadjusted intervals as simultaneous guarantees. Improvement after old replacement, supported by matched controls, strata, and intervention checks, supports only a checkpoint- and protocol-specific hypothesis. It does not validate unmet needs or guarantee benefits from older-prefix dropout. Keep the pinned host macro HR@10 as the sole selection criterion. Avoid repeated tuning to diagnostic outcomes; bound all added inference within the shared budget.

No training change or extra fitted predictor is required. Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, all four routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, and single-GPU execution. Load exactly one independently trained checkpoint per category. Any later training regularizer must preserve NextItNet and update the embedded predictor writer consistently. No supplied implementation or checkpoint was inspected, so padding and locality properties remain checks to perform, not findings.
idea.pseudocode:
save_mode = view.model.training
try:
  view.model.eval()
  tuples = cache_up_to_10_batches(train_loader)
  audit_dependency_graph_and_padding_when_accessible()
  with no_grad():
    for _, sequence, positive, negative in tuples:
      occupied = sequence != 0
      last = largest_original_occupied_index_per_row(occupied)
      exclude_empty_rows_and_invalid_aligned_targets_with_counts()
      candidates = stack(positive_at(last), negative_at(last))
      intact_features = gather(view.log2feats(sequence), last)
      intact_scores = view.predict_score(intact_features, candidates)
      verify_no_op_against_intact()
      for eligible_row in rows_with_recent_and_old_positions:
        m = min(3, count(lags_1_to_5), count(lags_at_least_16))
        for draw in three_fixed_seed_draws:
          positions = sample_matched_recent_old_random_positions(m)
          for replacement in [ID0, ZERO_INPUT_EMBEDDING, FREQUENCY_MATCHED_ITEM]:
            edited_features = diagnostic_forward(sequence, positions, replacement)
            edited_scores = view.predict_score(gather(edited_features, last), candidates)
            record_delta_of_positive_minus_negative_margin_and_counts()
      if audited_locality_and_occupied_positions_outside_field:
        verify_outside_field_feature_and_score_invariance()
  if exact_authorized_validation_candidates_available:
    repeat_prespecified_interventions_on_same_users_and_candidates()
    record_ranks_hits_hit_transitions_and_top10_overlap()
    average_replacement_draws_within_user()
    paired_stratified_user_bootstrap(replicates=2000, seed=42)
  else:
    mark_validation_metrics_missing_with_reason()
finally:
  remove_temporary_hooks()
  view.model.train(save_mode)
return {metrics: observations_counts_and_missing_reasons,
        metric_definitions: formulas_protocol_and_limitations}
# diagnosis_interpreter_prompt embeds both dictionaries and requests
# evidence-linked JSON findings without interpreting sensitivity as intent.

originality.positive: Integrates family-specific dependency auditing, controlled temporal interventions, and explicit missing-evidence reporting in a practical adapter.
originality.negative: Temporal ablation, matched controls, and bootstrap uncertainty are established methods; the contribution is their careful integration.

future_potential.positive: Can distinguish implementation artifacts from reproducible temporal sensitivity and motivate targeted NextItNet regularization.
future_potential.negative: Diagnostic sensitivity may not predict gains in validation HR@10, transfer across categories, or explain users’ actual choices.

code_difficulty.positive: Most measurements use existing hooks and require no retraining or additional fitted model.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable embedding interventions, complete locality auditing, fixed-candidate access, matched controls, and uncertainty reporting exceed a simple masking implementation.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Uses residual dilated causal convolutions for sequential recommendation.
Provides the architectural basis for temporal dependency and receptive-field analysis.
limitations: Architectural reach does not establish actual temporal sensitivity or user intent.
The supplied model’s block design, padding behavior, and normalization must be audited directly.

related_work.title: Interaction-removal study and finite rank-biased overlap
contributions: The supplied research summary reports greater degradation after removing recent training interactions.
Introduces finite rank-biased overlap for comparing finite recommendation lists.
limitations: Training-data removal does not establish frozen-model sensitivity to inference-time replacements.
The proposed diagnostic uses explicitly defined top-10 set overlap; FRBO would require its own published definition and parameters.

related_work.title: Usage-centric Intent Understanding
contributions: Examines intended use beyond rigid product categories and ambiguous descriptive properties.
Motivates distinguishing specific textual support from broad semantic similarity.
limitations: Does not validate task-specific recommendation proxies or establish satisfaction, compatibility, and unmet needs from histories.
The twenty feedback users and potentially sparse descriptions constrain relation-audit validation.

related_work.title: Computing Receptive Fields of Convolutional Neural Networks
contributions: Explains receptive-field calculations for convolutional computation graphs.
Supports counting every temporal convolution and combining dependencies across branches.
limitations: A convolution-only span is insufficient when other operations mix temporal positions.
Maximum span does not by itself identify holes in exact reachable positions or measure learned sensitivity.

related_work.title: ROAR: Evaluating Feature Importance Estimates
contributions: Uses removal and retraining to evaluate feature-importance estimates.
Motivates distinguishing frozen intervention effects from behavior after retraining.
limitations: Does not establish an optimal intervention for sequential recommendation.
Retraining would consume additional budget and answer a different question from the selected diagnostic.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Analyzes how candidate sampling affects recommendation metrics and comparisons.
Supports restricting conclusions to the pinned sampled-candidate protocol.
limitations: Does not justify modifying the host evaluator.
Full-catalog ranking still lacks complete relevance judgments.

related_work.title: RecBole NextItNet Implementation
contributions: Illustrates concrete residual blocks, biased convolutions, and feature-wise normalization.
Provides implementation examples motivating padding and activation controls.
limitations: An external implementation does not establish the supplied checkpoint’s architecture or padding semantics.

related_work.title: Statistical Significance Testing for Natural Language Processing
contributions: Provides guidance on statistical comparisons and the assumptions behind testing procedures.
Motivates paired comparisons and explicit reporting of exploratory analyses.
limitations: Does not independently validate the proposed recommendation bootstrap protocol.
User bootstrap intervals exclude training variability and adaptive validation overfitting.
